meta_title: OrthoAutoAI — AI spelling & grammar fixer for Windows and Linux
meta_description: Select text in any app, press Alt + C, and OrthoAutoAI fixes spelling and grammar with Google Gemini. Free, for Windows and Linux, in 7 languages.
og_tagline: Fix spelling & grammar in any app with one shortcut
hero_title: Fix spelling and grammar anywhere, with one shortcut.
hero_lead_html: Select text, press <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>, and OrthoAutoAI replaces it with the corrected version. Powered by Google Gemini.
hero_note: You'll need a free Gemini API key from Google.
demo_label: Example: a sentence with mistakes, corrected by OrthoAutoAI
features_title: A small tool that works wherever you type.
feat_universal_d: Browser, Word, Notepad, Discord, email, terminal: if you can select and paste text, OrthoAutoAI can fix it.
feat_ai_d: Google Gemini reads the whole sentence, so it fixes grammar and agreement, not just typos.
feat_lang_d: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese and Romanian, for both the interface and the corrections.
feat_history_d: Your last 5 corrections are kept in a dedicated tab, so you can get back what you had before.
feat_confirm_d: Turn on manual confirmation to check and edit the correction before it replaces your text.
feat_hotkeys_d: Change the correction and settings shortcuts, the confirmation sound and launch at startup.
how_title: Three steps, no copy-pasting into a chatbot.
how_key_d_html: Create a free API key in Google AI Studio and paste it into OrthoAutoAI on first launch. It is stored locally on your computer.
step1_d: Highlight the text you want to fix, in any window.
step3_d: The corrected text replaces your selection, in place.
linux_lead: A community port rewritten in Python and GTK4, with the same shortcuts, the same 7 languages and native Wayland support.
win_card_d: The original app, built with AutoHotkey.
win_li2: System tray icon and settings window
linux_card_d: Python 3.10+ and GTK4, no pip dependencies.
linux_li1: Wayland first: Hyprland, GNOME, KDE, Sway
linux_li2: X11 supported with a built-in hotkey daemon
linux_step2: Clone the repository and run the installer
linux_step3: Open the settings and paste your API key
linux_hint_html: Shortcuts are set up automatically on Hyprland. On GNOME, KDE or Sway, run orthoautoai install-hotkeys --print to get the right snippet. Something not working? orthoautoai doctor shows what was detected.
faq1_a: Yes. The app is free and its code is on GitHub. Corrections go through the Google Gemini API with your own key, and Google offers a free tier with usage limits.
faq2_q: Do I need a Gemini API key?
faq2_a_html: Yes. Create one for free in Google AI Studio, then paste it into OrthoAutoAI on first launch. It takes about a minute.
faq3_q: Which apps does it work in?
faq3_a: Any app where you can select, copy and paste text: browsers, Word, Notepad, Discord, email clients and more. On Linux terminals, set the copy and paste shortcuts to Ctrl + Shift + C / V in the advanced settings.
faq4_a: Only the text you select is sent to the Google Gemini API to be corrected. Your API key is stored in a local configuration file on your computer. OrthoAutoAI is not affiliated with Google.
faq5_a: Not for now. OrthoAutoAI is available for Windows and, through the community port, for Linux.
faq6_a: Yes. Alt + C corrects and Alt + W opens the settings by default, and both can be changed in the settings.
support_title: Found a bug or have an idea?
support_text: Open an issue on GitHub, for the Windows app as well as the Linux version.
footer_tagline: AI spelling and grammar fixer for Windows and Linux.
footer_disclaimer: Not affiliated with Google. Requires your own Gemini API key.
